clue.text: Striking show of appreciation — slow to disapprove

definitions.text: Striking show of appreciation — slow to disapprove

parts.words: Striking show of appreciation — slow to disapprove
parts.note: applause made by striking the palms together, which when done at a deliberately slow beat signals that an audience is unhappy

explanation.surface: Someone describes how a striking ovation turns into a protest when its pace drops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' is literal: the hands strike each other. In Britain a slow, rhythmic version of this applause is a recognised way for a crowd to show impatience or disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapping the hands together is the usual way an audience shows approval, and the slow version is the familiar sign of displeasure.

clue.text: Detectives following one into flat, say, revealing crime

indicators.note: into says the detectives and the one go inside the flat

parts.note: a flat is an example of a home

indicators.note: following places the detectives after the one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British detectives

explanation.surface: Police enter a flat after a man and discover a murder.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the plain-clothes detective branch of British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing a person is the gravest crime.

clue.text: Account arranged by being introduced to local resident

indicators.note: being introduced to says the abbreviation is put into the resident

parts.note: a native is a local resident
ARR is the abbreviation for arranged, as in music credits

explanation.surface: A story was set up by meeting someone who lives nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A story or report of events is an account.

clue.text: Make slow progress in Indian powwow initially

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Discussions at a tribal council inch forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To move very slowly and stealthily is to make slow progress.

clue.text: A scientist working hard finally gets leave

parts.note: BSc, Bachelor of Science, is a scientist's degree
on means working, functioning

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A diligent researcher at last earns time off.
explanation.definitionFit: To run away secretly is to leave, usually to escape something.

clue.text: The favourite could be a strange child

parts.note: strange means odd
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A punter muses that the race favourite might turn out to be an oddball offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, the runner priced at less than evens is the one most expected to win, the favourite.

clue.text: Uncertain girl presented with the token of love

parts.note: Di is a girl's name
a ring is given as a token of love

explanation.surface: A girl is given a lover's token but cannot decide.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitating, unable to make up one's mind, means uncertain.

clue.text: Tack grips when hammered

indicators.note: when hammered suggests the word is battered out of shape

explanation.surface: A tack holds fast once it is hammered in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tack' and 'hammered' paint carpentry; a sprig is a small headless tack.
explanation.definitionFit: A small nail without a head is a carpentry tack.

clue.text: Failed to attend, but allowed to pass

definitions.meaning: gave a nod of approval, let through

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is drowsing and losing attention; the other is approving something with a nod.

clue.text: Old watch list applied to harbour vessel

indicators.note: to harbour means to hold something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to list is to tip, lean over
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: An old seaman's watch log is pinned up for a harbour boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbour' and 'vessel' suggest shipping; harbour is the container instruction. A turnip was slang for a large old-fashioned pocket watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Large thick pocket watches were jokingly nicknamed after a root vegetable.

clue.text: Work unit in State combine

indicators.note: in tells us the work unit sits inside the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine
the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Two parts of a government office are being amalgamated.
explanation.definitionFit: To combine two things is to join them into one, a synonym.

clue.text: Screened in silence with spoken accompaniment

indicators.note: with says the spoken part comes along after the call for silence

parts.note: SH is the call for silence
uttered means spoken

explanation.surface: A film was shown in a hushed hall with a live narration alongside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screened' suggests showing a film, but here it means hidden behind shutters.
explanation.definitionFit: Windows closed off by shutters are screened from view, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Restriction making potato store lower

parts.note: a clamp is a heap of potatoes stored under straw and earth
down means lower, as in further down

explanation.surface: A farm rule forbids keeping the potato heap on lower ground.
explanation.walkthrough: A clamp is a farming term: root crops piled up and covered with earth to keep over winter.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackdown or tightening of rules is a restriction, a synonym.

clue.text: A high-flier chosen to represent US

definitions.meaning: a bird of prey that soars very high
the bald one is the national emblem of the United States

explanation.definitionFit: This raptor soars at great heights and was adopted as the symbol of America.

clue.text: Shed water, having ducked in river? On the contrary

indicators.note: in, read with the closing phrase, places one piece inside the other
on the contrary flips the order the clue states, so the river goes inside the ducking rather than the other way round

parts.note: ducked means dipped

explanation.surface: Someone is dripping wet after being dunked in a river, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, DIPPED would go inside R; 'On the contrary' reverses that, so R goes inside DIPPED.
explanation.definitionFit: Water falling off in drops has been let fall, or shed, by something wet.

clue.text: A main crop developed, taking the broad view

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters grow into a new form

explanation.surface: A principal harvest has grown, seen from a wide perspective.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweeping outlook covering a wide area takes in the broad view.

clue.text: Smartens up pair of little rascals

parts.note: imps are mischievous children

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up a couple of naughty children.
explanation.definitionFit: To tidy one's appearance fussily is to smarten up, a synonym.

clue.text: Pointed shape confined to fish

parts.note: pent means confined, as in pent up
to angle is to fish

explanation.surface: A star-shaped figure is trapped in a fish tank.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-pointed star is a figure with points.

clue.text: Chief vehicle noise a new driver creates?

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
din means noise
L is a learner, from the L-plate shown by a new driver

explanation.surface: A learner driver revs a car, making a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: British learner drivers display an L-plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Main or principal, as in cardinal points or sins, means chief.

clue.text: One tending to be less stout

definitions.meaning: one who inclines or leans towards something
thinner, comparative of an adjective for slim

explanation.definitionFit: One with a tendency or inclination leans, and a thinner person is less fat.

clue.text: Keep army in check

indicators.note: in places the army inside the check

parts.note: a rein is a check, a restraint
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A general orders the troops held back.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold on to something is to keep it.

clue.text: Bloomer's a big one, disastrously so

indicators.note: disastrously says these letters have come to grief and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits to a huge blunder that went terribly wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake, matching 'big one'; here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that bears flowers is a bloomer, and this is a popular flowering bedding plant.

clue.text: Most daring items of underwear

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear
a vest is an undershirt in British usage

explanation.surface: Someone describes the boldest lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is a sleeveless undershirt, not a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: The bravest person is the most courageous, most daring.

clue.text: Risky venture that's reduced one's hard cash

parts.note: spec is short for speculation, a risky venture
that is, reduced to its abbreviation, is IE (id est)

explanation.surface: A gamble has cut someone's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' looks like losses; it says 'that is' is shortened to IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Money in coin rather than notes is hard cash.

clue.text: Previous head of house

definitions.meaning: the superior of a religious house, a priory

explanation.definitionFit: An earlier event is one that came before, and the monk ranked under an abbot heads a religious community.

clue.text: Has occupier, so key's provided

definitions.meaning: ..., describing a property with a tenant
a key or cay is a small low island

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition gives two words, IS LET, run together.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny island is called a key in the Caribbean, and a tenanted property is let.

clue.text: Coach party for old militiamen

parts.note: to coach is to train
a band is a party or group of people

explanation.surface: A coach party sets off carrying veteran soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Trainbands were citizen militia companies in London from the 16th to 18th centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: These were historical companies of citizen soldiers, so old militia.

clue.text: Form of restraint — what a Piggy- Wig had?

parts.note: Edward Lear's Piggy-wig had a ring at the end of his nose: a ring shape O inside the word for nose

explanation.surface: A loop for tying up is compared to the pig in a nonsense poem.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lear's The Owl and the Pussy-cat, the Piggy-wig has a ring at the end of his nose; put O (ring) in NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: A running loop that tightens is a way of restraining an animal.

clue.text: Pass with hesitation and be in disarray as one played with Harlequin

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
um is a sound of hesitation

indicators.note: in disarray says the letters of the words before it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A muddled performer hesitates before going on stage alongside a clown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disarray' rearranges BE IN to give BINE. Columbine is Harlequin's sweetheart in the commedia dell'arte and English pantomime.
explanation.definitionFit: This stock character of the harlequinade is the beloved partner of Harlequin.

clue.text: Instrument of buccaneer's execution

indicators.note: execution suggests beheading, so the pirate loses his first letter

parts.note: Henry Morgan was a famous Welsh buccaneer

explanation.surface: A pirate's hanging is accompanied by a weapon or tool.
explanation.walkthrough: Beheading the buccaneer Morgan removes his head, the M.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe organ is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Attract some apprentices

indicators.note: some says only part of the following word is wanted

explanation.surface: A firm hopes to draw in a few trainees.
explanation.definitionFit: To lure someone with a promise is to attract them, a synonym.

clue.text: Highly delicate English leather given special treatment

indicators.note: given special treatment suggests the leather is worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: A fine English hide has been specially processed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leather' looks like the material being treated, but 'given special treatment' is the anagram signal working on that word alone, with English supplying only its initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something airy, light and unearthly is extremely delicate.
